methodology: To decompose both the original research topic and the generated technical specification into atomic units, I systematically analyzed each requirement, feature, and behavior described in both documents. The criteria for atomic units included independence (each unit should stand alone), technical specificity (each unit should be clear and unambiguous), and implementability (each unit should represent a single requirement that can be implemented). I carefully extracted key components from both texts, ensuring that each atomic unit captured a distinct aspect of the design requirements or specifications.
mindtraced_atomic_units: The design is a 64-bit arithmetic shift register.
The shift register has synchronous load capabilities.
The shift register can shift left by 1 bit when 'amount' is 2'b00.
The shift register can shift left by 8 bits when 'amount' is 2'b01.
The shift register can perform an arithmetic right shift by 1 bit when 'amount' is 2'b10.
The shift register can perform an arithmetic right shift by 8 bits when 'amount' is 2'b11.
The 'load' signal loads the shift register with data[63:0] instead of shifting when active high.
The 'ena' signal enables shifting when active high.
The output 'q' reflects the current contents of the shift register.
spec_atomic_units: The module implements a 64-bit arithmetic shift register with synchronous load capabilities.
The 'clk' signal triggers operations on the positive edge.
The 'load' signal allows loading of 'data' into 'q' when high.
The 'ena' signal enables shifting operations when high.
The 'amount' input determines the direction and magnitude of the shift.
When 'amount' is 2'b00, 'q' is shifted left by 1 bit.
When 'amount' is 2'b01, 'q' is shifted left by 8 bits.
When 'amount' is 2'b10, 'q' is arithmetic right shifted by 1 bit.
When 'amount' is 2'b11, 'q' is arithmetic right shifted by 8 bits.
The output 'q' is updated based on the 'load' and 'ena' signals.
The design prioritizes the load operation over shifting.
Non-blocking assignments are used for 'q' to ensure simultaneous updates at the clock edge.
